# WJPr

WJPr is an R package from the World Justice Project Data Analytics Unit
for producing WJP-style graphics and working with Rule of Law Index
data. It is designed for analysts who need publication-ready charts,
reproducible examples, and consistent visual language across
country-report and research workflows.

## Features

WJPr provides:

- Chart functions for bars (stacked or side by side), diverging bars,
  grouped bars, edge bars, funnels, dots, lines, slopes, dumbbells,
  lollipops, scatter plots, radar, rose, gauge, cards, heat maps,
  networks, UpSet diagrams, and sankey diagrams.
- Report-grade geometry:
  [`wjp_layout()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_layout.md)
  fixes label columns, tracks, rows, headers, and margins in points, and
  [`wjp_save()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_save.md)
  exports charts at their exact size, with SVG text converted to
  outlines and PNG at 300 dpi.
- Built-in sample datasets for Rule of Law Index and General Population
  Poll workflows.
- A shared WJP theme
  ([`WJP_theme()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/WJP_theme.md)),
  fonts
  ([`wjp_fonts()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_fonts.md),
  [`wjp_font_family()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_font_family.md)),
  color palettes
  ([`wjp_palette()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_palette.md),
  [`wjp_colors()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_palette.md)),
  and sequential scales
  ([`scale_fill_wjp_seq()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/scale_fill_wjp_seq.md))
  for consistent report graphics.
- [`wjp_drawn()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_drawn.md)
  to check the texts and marks a chart draws without rasterizing it.
- [`spread_labels_x()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/spread_labels_x.md),
  a deterministic helper that keeps value labels in row-based point
  charts from overlapping.
- Validation helpers for checking chart-ready data
  ([`wjp_check_data()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_check_data.md))
  and dependencies
  ([`wjp_check_deps()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_check_deps.md)),
  plus
  [`diffmeans()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/diffmeans.md)
  for difference-in-means tests.

## Installation

WJPr is hosted on GitHub. Install it with `remotes` (or `devtools`):

``` r

# Install WJPr from GitHub
remotes::install_github("worldjusticeproject/WJPr")
```

## Usage

Load the package into your R session:

``` r

library(WJPr)
```

### Example: Accessing Rule of Law Index Data

The package provides built-in datasets for analysis:

``` r

# View the first few rows of the dataset
head(WJPr::roli)
```

### Example: Creating a Visualization

Create a simple WJP-style bar chart:

``` r

library(dplyr)

# Load the WJP fonts before plotting
wjp_fonts()

# Prepare the data: % of respondents who trust Institution A, 2022
data4bars <- WJPr::gpp %>%
  filter(year == 2022) %>%
  mutate(
    q1a   = as.double(unclass(q1a)),  # survey answers are labelled vectors
    trust = case_when(q1a <= 2 ~ 1, q1a <= 4 ~ 0),
    year  = as.character(year)
  ) %>%
  group_by(country, year) %>%
  summarise(trust = mean(trust, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, .groups = "drop")

# Draw the chart
wjp_bars(
  data4bars,
  target   = "trust",
  grouping = "country",
  colors   = "year",
  cvec     = c("2022" = "#482d8b")
)
```

When `cvec` is omitted, every chart falls back to the WJP palette
([`wjp_palette()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_palette.md)).

### Example: Changing the Chart Font

[`wjp_fonts()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_fonts.md)
registers two font systems: **Lato** (the default, in Full, Light, and
Black weights) and **Inter Tight**. Switch every chart of the session
with the `wjpr.family` option:

``` r

# Load the WJP fonts (Lato + Inter Tight)
wjp_fonts()

# All charts use Lato by default
wjp_bars(data4bars, target = "trust", grouping = "country")

# Switch every chart to Inter Tight
options(wjpr.family = "Inter Tight")
wjp_bars(data4bars, target = "trust", grouping = "country")

# Check the active family at any time
wjp_font_family()
#> [1] "Inter Tight"

# Back to Lato
options(wjpr.family = NULL)
```

See
[`wjp_font_family()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_font_family.md)
for per-chart and theme-only alternatives.

### Example: Exporting a Report Figure

Register the static font files with systemfonts and save the chart at
its exact size, with the text of the SVG converted to outlines:

``` r

wjp_fonts(engine = "systemfonts")
options(wjpr.family = "Inter Tight")

p <- wjp_bars(
  data4bars, target = "trust", grouping = "country", direction = "horizontal",
  layout = wjp_layout(label_width = 120, track_width = 300, row_height = 22, bar_height = 18)
)
wjp_save(p, "trust.svg")                  # size of the layout, text as outlines
wjp_save(p, "trust.png", png_dpi = 300)
```

## Data Structure

All WJPr visualization functions expect data in **long (tidy) format**:

    | grouping     | target | colors   | labels (optional) |
    |--------------|--------|----------|-------------------|
    | Category A   | 45.2   | Group 1  | "45%"             |
    | Category B   | 32.1   | Group 1  | "32%"             |
    | Category A   | 51.0   | Group 2  | "51%"             |
    | Category B   | 38.5   | Group 2  | "39%"             |

**Key parameters used across all functions:**

| Parameter  | Description                           | Type              |
|------------|---------------------------------------|-------------------|
| `target`   | Values to plot (Y-axis)               | Numeric column    |
| `grouping` | Categories (X-axis or rows)           | Character/Factor  |
| `colors`   | Variable for color grouping           | Character/Factor  |
| `cvec`     | Named vector mapping values to colors | `c("A" = "#HEX")` |
| `labels`   | Text labels to display                | Character column  |

### Validate Your Data

Use
[`wjp_check_data()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_check_data.md)
to verify your data structure before plotting:

``` r

wjp_check_data(
  data     = my_data,
  type     = "bars",
  target   = "value",
  grouping = "category",
  colors   = "group",
  cvec     = c("Group 1" = "#482d8b", "Group 2" = "#2894aa")
)
```

For detailed guidance, see the [Data Preparation
vignette](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/articles/data-preparation.html).

## Documentation

Comprehensive documentation is available for all functions and datasets.
Use the R help system to access it:

``` r

?WJPr::wjp_lines
```

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Before contributing, please read our
guidelines:

### Quick Start

1.  Fork the repository
2.  Create a feature branch: `git checkout -b feature/new-chart`
3.  Follow the coding conventions in
    [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/CONTRIBUTING.md)
4.  Submit a pull request

### Adding New Functions

All visualization functions must follow the WJPr patterns:

``` r

wjp_newchart <- function(
    data,
    target,
    grouping,
    colors    = NULL,
    cvec      = NULL,
    labels    = NULL,
    ptheme    = WJP_theme()
) {
  # 1. Rename columns using all_of()
  # 2. Handle NULL parameters
  # 3. Fall back to the WJP palette when cvec is NULL (wjp_default_cvec())
  # 4. Create ggplot, using wjp_font_family() for text layers
  # 5. Apply ptheme, then chart-specific theme() tweaks
  return(plt)
}
```

### Documentation Requirements

- Roxygen2 with `@export`, `@param`, `@return`, `@examples`
- Include `lifecycle::badge("experimental")` in description
- Add tests in `tests/testthat/` and an example to
  `data-raw/generate-examples.R`
- Register the function in `_pkgdown.yml` and update `NEWS.md`

### Resources

- **[CONTRIBUTING.md](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/CONTRIBUTING.md)** -
  Complete contribution guidelines
- **[Development
  Guide](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/articles/development-guide.html)** -
  Step-by-step tutorial
- **[Issues](https://github.com/worldjusticeproject/WJPr/issues)** -
  Report bugs or request features

# Package index

## Bars

Functions for vertical, horizontal, diverging, grouped, edge, and funnel
bar charts.

- [`wjp_bars()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_bars.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Plot a Bar Chart following WJP style guidelines
- [`wjp_divbars()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_divbars.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Plot a Diverging Horizontal Bar Chart following
  WJP style guidelines
- [`wjp_groupbars()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_groupbars.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Plot a Grouped Stacked Bar Chart following WJP
  style guidelines
- [`wjp_edgebars()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_edgebars.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Plot a Horizontal Edgebars Chart following WJP
  style guidelines
- [`wjp_funnel()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_funnel.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Plot a Funnel Chart following WJP style
  guidelines

## Dots and Lines

Functions for comparing points, trends, slopes, changes, lollipops, and
scatter plots.

- [`wjp_dots()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_dots.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Plot a Dots Chart following WJP style
  guidelines
- [`wjp_lines()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_lines.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Plot a Line Chart following WJP style
  guidelines
- [`wjp_slope()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_slope.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Plot a Slope Chart following WJP style
  guidelines
- [`wjp_dumbbells()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_dumbbells.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Plot a Dumbbell Chart following WJP style
  guidelines
- [`wjp_lollipops()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_lollipops.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Plot a Lollipop Chart following WJP style
  guidelines
- [`wjp_scatter()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_scatter.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Plot a Scatter Chart following WJP style
  guidelines

## Radial and Special

Functions for radial charts, rose charts, and gauges.

- [`wjp_radar()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_radar.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Plot a Radar Chart following WJP style
  guidelines
- [`wjp_rose()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_rose.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Plot a Rose Chart following WJP style
  guidelines
- [`wjp_gauge()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_gauge.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Plot a Gauge Chart following WJP style
  guidelines

## Tables, Matrices, and Flows

Functions for cards, heat maps, networks, set intersections (UpSet), and
sankey diagrams.

- [`wjp_cards()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_cards.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Plot Score Cards following WJP style guidelines
- [`wjp_heatmap()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_heatmap.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Plot a Heat Map following WJP style guidelines
- [`wjp_network()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_network.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Plot a Network Chart following WJP style
  guidelines
- [`wjp_upset()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_upset.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Plot an UpSet Chart following WJP style
  guidelines
- [`wjp_sankey()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_sankey.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Plot a Sankey Diagram following WJP style
  guidelines

## Layout and Export

Geometry in points, export at an exact size with text outlines, and
verification of what a chart draws.

- [`wjp_layout()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_layout.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Chart Geometry in Points
- [`wjp_save()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_save.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Save a WJP Chart at Its Exact Size
- [`wjp_drawn()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_drawn.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Texts and Marks Drawn by a Chart

## Validation, Analysis, and Styling

Support tools for validating data, checking dependencies, analyzing
differences, spreading overlapping labels, and applying WJP styling.

- [`wjp_check_data()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_check_data.md)
  : Validate Data Structure for WJPr Charts
- [`wjp_check_deps()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_check_deps.md)
  : Check WJPr Dependencies
- [`diffmeans()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/diffmeans.md)
  : Difference of Means Analysis
- [`wjp_fonts()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_fonts.md)
  : Load WJP Fonts
- [`wjp_font_family()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_font_family.md)
  : Get the Active WJP Font Family
- [`wjp_palette()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_palette.md)
  [`wjp_colors()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/wjp_palette.md)
  : WJP Color Palettes
- [`scale_fill_wjp_seq()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/scale_fill_wjp_seq.md)
  [`scale_colour_wjp_seq()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/scale_fill_wjp_seq.md)
  [`scale_color_wjp_seq()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/scale_fill_wjp_seq.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Sequential WJP Color Scales
- [`spread_labels_x()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/spread_labels_x.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Spread overlapping point labels horizontally
- [`WJP_theme()`](https://worldjusticeproject.github.io/WJPr/reference/WJP_theme.md)
  : WJP ggplot2 Theme

  GPP Sample Data
